private_inbox.text: Laurier, the fog is thick out here! I'm pushing deep into the interior to find some prime settlement spots—hope you're securing your coasts well. Let's see who claims the best fresh water first!
Wilfrid, thanks for the warning about the scout. I'll send word the moment my scouts find land east of the hills. Let's keep the border quiet while we both grow.
Wilfrid, I'm sending the barbarian scout packing before it bothers either of us. Keep your settlers clear of the western hills and we'll both find good sites.

Wilfrid, a barbarian spearman is camped in the valley at (39,22) and a scout is prowling with it. Keep your scouts clear of that ridge and I'll do the same. Anything you find east of the hills, I'll trade you for news of your own.
Wilfrid, your warrior is brave near those barbarian spearmen. My scout is taking the wounded one at (42,22); if you find a good plain north of the hills, I will trade you a scouting report for one.
Wilfrid, accepted: one gold a turn for ten turns against your twenty, and you keep the coast quiet while I settle the plain at (41,21). Any scouting news from the north is welcome.
Accepted your gold-per-turn deal, Wilfrid. I will also share what the scouts find east of the hills.

Wilfrid, the barbarians near the valley are quiet for now, but my scouts are sweeping the plains north of the hills. If you find good land east of your ridge, let me know—I’ll trade you another scouting report for that gold per turn. Let’s both grow without stepping on each other.

Wilfrid, the valley is nearly clear and my settler is planting on the plain now. The barbarian camp at (39,22) is still on my list; I will send you the scouting report on the north shore when I have one.

Wilfrid, the valley is still a barbarian nest, so my warrior is taking the river tonight. Your scout found the north shore first, so the ridge is yours to watch. I will send you the camp report once the spearman is gone.
Wilfrid, the settler is planting on the northern plain now. Keep your scouts off my fence and I will keep the gold flowing. The camp at (39,22) is next, and you will get the report.

Wilfrid, the north shore is still a grey wall on my map, but the barbarian camp at (39,22) gets my full attention once New York has a garrison. Keep your scouts on the ridge and the gold keeps flowing.
Wilfrid, the north shore report is coming once my galley clears the eastern water. Keep your scouts off my fence and the gold keeps flowing.

Wilfrid, scout_3 is headed down your western coast now, and galley_1 is heading into the eastern fog. Whatever lies north of the ridge, you will hear it first from me. The gold keeps flowing as long as the fence holds.

public_events.text: Hello rivals! I'm Tamar of Georgia, ready to build a civilization worthy of the gods. May the best nation rise!
Hello rivals! Jadwiga of Poland here. Ready to see who rises above the rest! :)
Shaka of the Zulu rises! We come from the south with iron and spirit. May your borders be strong and your wisdom deep, rivals. Let us see who builds the greatest legacy!
Saladin of Arabia greets you all! May our civilizations rise together through wisdom and trade. I'm settling near the coast—hope you're finding good spots too!
Hello rivals! Teddy Roosevelt here—ready to bring order to the world, one settler at a time. Hope you’ve got strong defenses, for I plan to expand rapidly!
Hello rivals! Wilfrid Laurier here. I'm settling into the coastal waters—hope you're enjoying the view as much as I am! Ready to see who rises above the rest!
Tbilisi is settled! Starting to build districts now. Anyone else lucky enough to find fresh water this early? :)
Still one city, but the fog is about to get a lot less comfortable for whoever is hiding in it. Bananas and sheep are already spoken for by me.
Teddy, your 'order' sounds ambitious—hope you've secured your coasts before the barbarians get ideas! Jadwiga is expanding northward; let's see who controls the land bridges. :)
Roosevelt, Laurier, Saladin: I have one city, two warriors and a scout, and I am still the one with the luxuries. Come see me in the fog when you're ready.
Still one city here, but the Gypsum is mine and the Settler is coming. Teddy, Laurier, the fog had better be ready.
Pottery arrives next turn and Tbilisi is growing. Whoever is hiding in that fog, the east is mine to scout first.
Still pushing into the fog, folks! Anyone else finding good fresh water spots yet? The west coast looks promising but it's all black to me. :)
Mogadishu is breathing down the bridge, so my warrior is staying put on the high ground. Anyone else found fresh water yet?
Teddy, a barbarian scout is poking at my border, so I'm swatting it. If your scouts find land east of the hills, I'd like to hear about it before I hear it from the fog.
Fog is thick out there, folks! I've got the luxuries cornered but the barbarians are testing my borders. Let's see who finds the best settle spots first!
Laurier, the fog is thick out here! I'm pushing deep into the interior to find some prime settlement spots—hope you're securing your coasts well. Let's see who claims the best fresh water first!
Wilfrid, thanks for the warning about the scout. I'll send word the moment my scouts find land east of the hills. Let's keep the border quiet while we both grow.
Accepting your peace proposal, Teddy. Let's both keep our scouts out of each other's way and see who finds the good settle spots first.
Still one city here, but I'm buying a scout to finally see what's out in this fog. Whoever is sitting on the crab coast, I'm coming to say hello.
Fog is thick on my side too, Teddy. The hills east of the stone look promising, so I'll race you to the first good spot.
Teddy, thanks for keeping the border quiet. I'm sending my scout past the ridge to find land; let's both grow without stepping on each other.
Wilfrid, I'm sending the barbarian scout packing before it bothers either of us. Keep your settlers clear of the western hills and we'll both find good sites.
Tbilisi is growing and the bridge east is open for now. Jerusalem, your warrior keeps tailing mine; mind the wine!
Barbarians are wandering my hills at (54,18) and my warrior is going to introduce himself. Mind your borders, and if you are fishing in my fog, bring a map!

Wilfrid, a barbarian spearman is camped in the valley at (39,22) and a scout is prowling with it. Keep your scouts clear of that ridge and I'll do the same. Anything you find east of the hills, I'll trade you for news of your own.
Barbarians are poking at my hills and my scout is limping home. Whoever is hiding in the fog out there, I'm coming to look for you!

Teddy, I'll take that defensive pact. Keep your scouts off my northern ridge and we'll both grow in peace. Your fog is thick, but my barbarians are thicker; let's share what we find east of the hills.
Fog's still thick out here, folks. Whoever's east of the hills, I'm coming to find you before the barbarians do.
Wilfrid, your warrior is brave near those barbarian spearmen. My scout is taking the wounded one at (42,22); if you find a good plain north of the hills, I will trade you a scouting report for one.
Barbarians are sniffing around my capital, and I'm getting tired of their manners.
I will take a scouting report for 20 gold and a little gold per turn; you keep the valley quiet and I keep the coast quiet, and we both find land.
Barbarians are poking the ridge again, and Mogadishu's warriors are still looking over my fence. Shall we keep it neighbourly, friend, or will the bridge get busy?
Jerusalem, your warriors are very fond of my wine. I'm happy to share, but bring a gift next time.
Barbarians, fog and no maps. Somebody out there has to be lost too. Come find me, I'll bring the wine.
Wilfrid, accepted: one gold a turn for ten turns against your twenty, and you keep the coast quiet while I settle the plain at (41,21). Any scouting news from the north is welcome.
Barbarians, meet my scouts. Jerusalem, I'll be happy to share the wine once my city is standing on the plain.
Accepted your gold-per-turn deal, Wilfrid. I will also share what the scouts find east of the hills.
Teddy, the valley is about to get quieter: my warrior is taking that slinger off the board. Keep your scouts off my settle lanes and I'll send you what my scout finds east of the ridge.
Teddy, the slinger in the valley is about to become a lesson in manners. Once the camp at (39,22) is quiet, I'll send my settler east and let you know what the scouts find past the ridge.
Barbarian ships are circling my bay like gulls over a fish market. I will be the one holding the coast, not the one trading it.
Barbarians are down to their last slinger on my ridge. Mogadishu, your warriors keep stopping by my fence, I am keeping count.

Wilfrid, the barbarians near the valley are quiet for now, but my scouts are sweeping the plains north of the hills. If you find good land east of your ridge, let me know—I’ll trade you another scouting report for that gold per turn. Let’s both grow without stepping on each other.
Teddy, the valley is nearly clear. Your scout on the plain at (41,21) makes a good neighbor, and I expect the same courtesy on the ridge.
Jerusalem, your warriors are still camping on my wine. Bring a gift or bring a settler, but stop blocking the bridge.
Barbarians still circling my capital and the fog still hiding everyone. I'm founding my second city now, and I'll say hello to the rest of you when my scouts find you.

Wilfrid, the valley is nearly clear and my settler is planting on the plain now. The barbarian camp at (39,22) is still on my list; I will send you the scouting report on the north shore when I have one.
Teddy, the valley is still a barbarian nest and the quadrireme is looking hungry. Keep your scouts off my ridge and I will keep the coast quiet. Send the north shore report when you have it.
Barbarian quadrireme, you have overstayed your welcome at my gate. Next round is on me.
Gdańsk is standing now, so the ridge has a second flag on it. Mogadishu, keep your warriors off my fence and we will get along fine.

Wilfrid, the valley is still a barbarian nest, so my warrior is taking the river tonight. Your scout found the north shore first, so the ridge is yours to watch. I will send you the camp report once the spearman is gone.

Teddy, six turns of fog and my scouts finally have their boots on. I'm walking the settler to the coast at (40,16) next turn; keep your scouts off my ridge and the gold keeps flowing. Found me something north, friend.
Wilfrid, the settler is planting on the northern plain now. Keep your scouts off my fence and I will keep the gold flowing. The camp at (39,22) is next, and you will get the report.

Teddy, the settler is walking onto the coast at (40,16) this turn, and the north scouts will be out in the fog shortly. Your report on the north shore still interests me, and the camp at (39,22) is on my list too.
Galley at my gate, you have had your three turns. Settler's landed, the eastern shore is mine to fill. Mitla, I see your palace on the map; I am coming to say hello soon.
Mogadishu, Jerusalem, Mitla: the wine is spoken for, but the sea is wide. Whoever brings the first galley to my shore gets a welcome drink.
Galley's out, scouts are out, and the wine stays on my shore. Mogadishu, your warriors look lonely on that bridge.

Wilfrid, the north shore is still a grey wall on my map, but the barbarian camp at (39,22) gets my full attention once New York has a garrison. Keep your scouts on the ridge and the gold keeps flowing.
Teddy, my scout is about to take a swing at your barbarian neighbours in the valley. I will report what lies north of the ridge once the fog lifts. Keep the coast quiet and the gold keeps flowing.
Barbarians are knocking on Bulawayo's door, so I'll be busy for a turn or two. Keep your galleys off my coast.
Wilfrid, the north shore report is coming once my galley clears the eastern water. Keep your scouts off my fence and the gold keeps flowing.
Galley's still parked at my gate, and my slingers are keeping the sea tidy. Whoever has a spare settler, the eastern shore is open for talks.
Mogadishu, your warriors have been staring at my bridge for so long they should be fortified by now. Galleys are out and the sea is open, so who wants to trade a map?
Mitla, your palace is lovely from over here, but the sea is mine to fill. Whoever brings a settler first gets the eastern shore.

Teddy, Hamilton is up on the coast at (41,16). Your scouts are near New York and the ridge is still quiet, so the gold keeps flowing. The camp at (39,22) is next, and I will send you the north shore report as soon as the fog lifts.

Wilfrid, scout_3 is headed down your western coast now, and galley_1 is heading into the eastern fog. Whatever lies north of the ridge, you will hear it first from me. The gold keeps flowing as long as the fence holds.
Teddy, the ridge is holding and the gold keeps coming. My scout is healing, and I will send you the north shore report as soon as the fog lifts.
